So a highly desirable feature of libpldm's APIs is they don't allocate, as it makes the library much easier to exploit in free-standing contexts. It's already the case that many of the APIs don't allocate, but I don't think we'd written that desire down anywhere. To that end I've created the following change:

[docs: checklists: Document heap allocation constraint](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/77509)

Can you please rework your design to not require heap allocation?

+1 to this.

I think we have two options (Andrew also pointed out the same):
1) Let caller do all the allocation (needs some assumptions about sizes or hints from the library).

2) (I would prefer this) - define structures/APIs for fixed vs variable parts and have the caller invoke APIs as relevant. For example - for the header you can define a structure until the PackageVersionStringLength and have a C flexible array member for the string itself. The caller can then invoke a different API, passing in a buffer large enough to hold the string (as the caller knows the string length from the prior API call to parse the header), to retrieve the string.
For variable sized entries, you could do something similar and have iterators (also suggested by Andrew elsewhere in this patchset iirc) to get the next item of something (similar to how readdir() etc. work).

I would also suggest looking at https://kernel.googlesource.com/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/mark/linux/+/refs/tags/arm64-ftrace-minimal-regs-20221103/lib/pldmfw for reference. This does do iterators but doesn't expose them as APIs. I also like this in terms of the structuring of the main parsing function two four parts - parse_header, parse_records, parse_components, verify_crc. These can be the public APIs, as iterator APIs though (get_next_component, etc.).

@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au does the above make sense to you? Would like to hear your thougts before we rework.

> and have a C flexible array member for the string itself.

Please be cautious about recommending flexible array members, they cause API trouble:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/059684c86558a638c19a64d4f2e4c5bd9a6e87f1/docs/checklists/changes.md#L154-L173

> These can be the public APIs, as iterator APIs though (get_next_component, etc.).

I prefer we follow the pattern I've set with the `foreach_*` macros as they hide a lot of the pain and provide consistency.

Note that the iterators I've defined so far use a `void *` pointing back into the message buffer for string data. The caller needs to copy the string data out and parse it themselves, with their own choice of library: the encoding and alignment are defined by other struct members and I don't want libpldm to prescribe string parsing implementations for its users.
Sounds good to me.
